Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp's Q3 2023 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are David Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Harper, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to David Reynolds.

David Reynolds: Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp delivered solid results in Q3, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved record production volumes averaging 275,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 10% sequentially and 15% year-over-year. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on realized pricing, bolstered by our effective hedging programs that provided significant uplift amid market volatility. We are focused on our production guidance for the coming periods, emphasizing capital-efficient growth from premium inventory. Finally, we are taking steps to further strengthen our environmental performance, with notable reductions in spills and incidents through proactive remediation and monitoring initiatives.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez to discuss our financial results in more detail.

John Ramirez: Thank you, David. As David mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.85 billion, up 18% year-over-year. Operating income was $925 million, and net income was $680 million. We generated $780 million in free cash flow and returned $420 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $5.2 billion in debt and $1.4 billion in cash.

Turning now to our realized pricing performance, which highlights the strength of our hedging discipline in a volatile macro environment. In the quarter, our realized oil price averaged $74.25 per barrel, while natural gas came in at $2.42 per MCF. These results showed sequential gains from Q2's $71.80 oil and $2.18 gas, supported by slightly stronger benchmarks and the benefits from our hedging efforts. Compared to last year, oil realizations rose 8% from $68.75, although gas declined 12% from $2.75 due to ongoing oversupply pressures in major basins.

Diving deeper into crude oil, the Q3 realized price of $74.25 per barrel was about 3% below the NYMEX WTI average settle of $76.85, mainly due to a $2.10 per barrel Permian basis differential, which improved from Q2's $2.85 discount thanks to added takeaway capacity from the Matterhorn Express Pipeline and EPIC Crude Oil Pipeline expansions. Roughly 65% of our Permian WTI barrels loaded at Corpus Christi reached parity with Argus WTI Houston, aided by LLS spreads over WTI averaging a $1.50 premium in Q3, up from $0.80 in the prior quarter. Meanwhile, our light sweet Eagle Ford output captured a $1.20 premium to WTI, realizing $78.45, owing to direct connections to the Eagle Ford Pipeline system supplying Houston refineries seeking low-sulfur grades to meet IMO 2020 compliance and LSFO demand.

On the natural gas side, pricing held firm at $2.42 per MCF, which was 5% above the Henry Hub average of $2.30, reflecting our advantageous positioning. In the Permian Delaware Basin, accounting for 70% of our gas output, the Waha Hub saw a $0.35 discount to Henry Hub—our tightest in three quarters—helped by the Whistler Pipeline reaching full operations and increased NET Mexico exports that absorbed associated gas and reduced flaring. Eagle Ford gas fetched $2.65 per MCF, a $0.25 premium, driven by strong Southeast Texas demand from LNG developments like Golden Pass and Plaquemines. Our overall blended gas realization gained from a 15% year-over-year drop in Permian shrinkage to 8%, achieved through better field compression and vapor recovery units.

The real value shines through in our hedging programs. Heading into Q3, we had 62% of oil production protected through a mix of swaps and three-way collars—swaps on 35% at a weighted average floor of $72.50 per barrel, collars at $68-$78-$88 for 20%, and puts at $70 for the rest. This added $4.75 per barrel to our oil realization, a 7% lift over the unhedged $69.50 that would have resulted from WTI dips to $72 amid OPEC+ compliance doubts and Hurricane Idalia effects. Importantly, the collars captured $2.10 per barrel in upside from the mid-September Brent rally to $78 triggered by Saudi voluntary cuts, illustrating the benefits of these costless structures.

For natural gas, with 55% hedged mainly via NYMEX Henry Hub swaps at $2.60 and basis swaps fixing Waha at -$0.20, we gained a $0.32 per MCF boost, elevating potential sub-$2.10 realizations to $2.42. This proved vital as Henry Hub volatility rose 25% during the quarter due to storage builds surpassing EIA forecasts by 12 Bcf.

In total, hedging safeguarded 68% of our hydrocarbon revenue in Q3, protecting EBITDA by roughly $185 million from a downside case of $70 WTI and $2.00 Henry Hub. Our approach stays conservative but flexible: we've added 58% coverage for Q4 2023 at $73 oil swaps, 52% for 2024 at $71.50 including 25% two-way collars at $65-$80, and 35% for 2025 at $70—all tied to NYMEX WTI with Permian basis swaps on 40% of volumes. This setup defends us against risks such as extended Russia-Ukraine supply issues, softer China demand, or faster U.S. shale expansion if Permian rig counts climb back toward 600.

With the Permian now comprising 82% of production following our $450 million Delaware bolt-on acquisition, this resilience is enhanced, as D&C efficiencies improved 12% year-over-year to maintain breakevens at $42 per barrel WTI equivalent. We're also progressing carbon capture links with Occidental's STRATOS project to access 45Q credits, which could deliver $5-7 per MCF uplift on associated gas by 2025.

Overall, these realized prices demonstrate how proactive hedging works in a backwardated WTI curve dropping 5% through 2024, while our asset quality and infrastructure yield premium captures. This supports our full-year outlook of $72-75 oil and $2.30-2.50 gas realized, with hedges offering solid protection.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Harper for an operational update.

Lisa Harper: Thank you, John. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 275,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought 27 new Delaware Basin wells online, which are expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives.

Before diving deeper into the financials earlier, let me expand on our production volumes this quarter. I'm pleased to report robust execution, with total output averaging 275,000 BOE per day in Q3, a 10% quarter-over-quarter increase from 250,000 BOE per day in Q2 and 15% year-over-year growth from 239,000 BOE per day in Q3 2022. This beat expectations thanks to our $1.2 billion 2024 drilling and completion capital program, focused on Tier 1 acreage in the Permian Basin, where we've refined our drilling inventory for 12,000-foot laterals and enhanced completions using 3,000 pounds of proppant per foot.

By commodity, oil production reached a record 175,000 barrels per day, rising 13% sequentially from 155,000 barrels per day in Q2 and 20% year-over-year from 146,000 barrels per day. The bulk came from those 27 new Delaware Basin wells in the core Waha-MVP area, where our four simul-frac crews sped completions by 25% ahead of schedule. These wells posted initial rates of 1,800 BOE per day, 65% oil, exceeding our type curve by 15% due to proprietary diverter tech and intense slickwater fracs. Midland Basin workovers on our 150-well inventory added 5,000 barrels per day, countering just 4% sequential declines in core assets.

Natural gas averaged 6.2 Bcf per day, equivalent to 103,000 BOE per day on a 6:1 MCF-to-BOE basis—flat quarter-over-quarter but up 5% year-over-year from 5.9 Bcf per day. We intentionally curtailed volumes amid softer $2.45 per MMBtu Henry Hub pricing versus $2.75 last year, holding back eight associated gas wells in the Permian for Q4 when Waha differentials should narrow after Freeport LNG ramps up. Our hedged gas floor at $2.50 per MMBtu covers 60% of Q4. Eagle Ford held steady at 1.1 Bcf per day, improved by DUC conversions and ESP artificial lift that boosted runtimes 10% and cut LOE by $1.50 per BOE.

By region, the Permian drove 82% of volumes at 225,000 BOE per day, up 12% sequentially, with D&C costs down to $650 per foot via supply chain gains and midstream deals with Enterprise and Crestwood. Bakken legacy declines of 3% to 25,000 BOE per day were offset by our $200 million bolt-on of 10,000 net acres in McKenzie County, adding 8,000 BOE per day. Eagle Ford showed promise from our condensate-rich Pearsall Shale pilot, with four test wells at 70% liquids and IPs over 1,200 BOE per day.

These outcomes validate our capital-efficient model, aiming for 8-10% annual growth through 2026 with free cash flow yields over 15% at $70 WTI. We've tightened full-year guidance to 268,000-278,000 BOE per day from 265,000-280,000, based on superior well results and fewer weather hits than Q2's Texas freeze. Moving forward, 70% of capex goes to Permian development, drawing on 5+ years of Tier 1 inventory at sub-$50 per BOE breakevens, plus bolt-ons like our recent Devon swap to optimize the portfolio. This keeps us ahead on returns in a $65-75 WTI environment.

Shifting to production guidance for Q4 2023 and full-year 2024, we're committed to discipline while pursuing organic growth from high-return inventory. For Q4, we project 850,000 to 875,000 BOE per day, a modest sequential pullback from Q3's 875,000 due to planned Gulf of Mexico platform turnarounds and North Sea weather deferrals. Oil is guided at 550,000 to 575,000 barrels per day, NGLs at 120,000 to 130,000 barrels per day, and gas at 1.1 to 1.15 Bcf per day—a 5% oil drop mainly from the 30-day Thunder Horse field turnaround, where subsea tiebacks and compression upgrades will add 15,000 BOE per day from Q1 2024.

For full-year 2024, we anticipate 1.20 to 1.25 million BOE per day, up 12% at midpoint from 2023's 1.08 million. That includes 775,000 to 825,000 barrels per day oil, 175,000 to 190,000 barrels per day NGLs, and 1.45 to 1.55 Bcf per day gas—15% oil growth led by Permian ramp. This aligns with our five-year 5%+ CAGR plan using low-breakeven inventory, without needing M&A.

Influencing factors include execution, markets, and strategies. In the Permian (52% of 2024 volumes), we guide 650,000 to 675,000 BOE per day, up 18% year-over-year, via 12 new Super Wolfbone pads with 12,000-foot laterals, 50-stage fracs, and first-month IPs of 1,800 BOE per day projecting 1.2 MMBoe EUR per well. D&C costs fell 15% to $7.5 million per well with walking rigs and AI frac scheduling cutting cycles 20%. We're running 22 rigs and 4 frac fleets on 4,500+ locations at sub-$40 WTI returns, aided by OPEC+ support for $75-85 per barrel Brent.

Eagle Ford and Bakken combined (15%) guide flat to +2% at 150,000 to 155,000 BOE per day, with Eagle Ford condensate benefiting from 40-stage fracs improving EURs 25% and Bakken EOR pilots targeting 10% recovery gains. Gulf deepwater (20%) eyes 220,000 to 240,000 BOE per day, up 10%, with Winterfell first oil adding 25,000 BOE per day at 15% IRR and two Chevron Anchor-style sidetracks. International (13%) holds 140,000 to 150,000 BOE per day, boosted by Guyana's Payara Phase 2, Brazil pre-salt FPSO #3, and North Sea offsets.

Upside from digital twins on 80% assets lifting uptime to 96% for 3-5% adds; EOR like Permian CO2 and Bakken polymers for 12% recovery; low-carbon methane cuts to 0.8 kg/BOE for CCUS credits. Headwinds: $10 WTI drop trims 50,000 BOE per day; permitting slips 2 rigs; 5% service inflation; hurricanes defer 10-20,000 BOE per day; ESG caps flaring. LNG surges lift gas 15%, but EVs limit gasoline growth.

We prioritize FCF, greenlighting only >15% IRR projects with $2.5-2.6 billion capex yielding 20%+ FCF at midpoint, all returned via buybacks and $1.20 per share dividend.

Finally, on environmental performance around spills, incidents, and remediation, our operations in Permian, Gulf of Mexico, and Eagle Ford emphasize zero-harm stewardship essential for our license, ESG goals, and shareholder value. Q3 capped our safest year, with big strides versus targets and peers.

We recorded 12 reportable spills, down 52% from 25 in 2022, via predictive maintenance and real-time monitoring. Total hydrocarbons spilled: 420 barrels, 65% less than 1,200 last year, for a 0.12 barrels per million production barrels rate—better than API's 0.45 upstream average and Exxon's 0.28. Seventy-five percent were Tier 1/2 like small flowline leaks; two Tier 3.

Regionally: Permian seven spills (180 barrels) from saltwater lines, down 40% volume with Chevron-style acoustic detection. Gulf three (120 barrels) from bilge during Idalia prep, at 0.08 bbl/MMboe beating Shell. Eagle Ford two (120 barrels), no aquifer hits per audits.

Remediation excelled: 14-hour average response inside 24-hour KPI; 98.7% recovered on-site using Viking skimmers/booms (60%), Corexit dispersants (25%), PetroCleanse microbes. Costs $28 million (15% of $185 million env capex), down 20% per barrel; all sites closed in 90 days, TPH under 100 ppm.

Five-year trends: 72% fewer spills, 81% less volume, beating IOGP. Driven by $45 million in JewelSuite digital twins for 80% pipelines, raising MTBF to 2,100 days via CUI prediction; FLIR drones/Planet satellites averting 800 barrels; 100% workforce STOP/VR training cutting errors 35%.

This boosted our S&P CSA environmental ranking to top quintile, aiding $2.5 billion green bond at 75 bps tighter. Prevention saved $150 million. For 2024, targeting <0.10 rate with $200 million capex for CCUS, SLB AquaTrak, Nature Conservancy offsets—supporting 2035 net-zero Scope 1/2.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Brian Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Brian Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the realized prices and the impact of your hedging programs this quarter?

David Reynolds: Good morning, Brian. As John outlined, our hedging was pivotal, adding $4.75 per barrel to oil and $0.32 per MCF to gas, protecting against volatility from OPEC+ uncertainty and weather events. With 62% oil hedged via swaps and collars, we captured upside too, and our forward layers at 58% for Q4 keep us buffered. It's core to our strategy in this environment.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen: Good morning. What are your expectations for production guidance next quarter and full year, including key factors?

John Ramirez: Morning, Laura. Lisa covered it well, but to reiterate, Q4 at 850,000-875,000 BOE per day accounts for turnarounds, with 2024 at 1.20-1.25 million reflecting Permian growth and tech upside like digital optimization. Risks like volatility or regs are hedged where possible, but our >15% IRR discipline ensures FCF focus—no volume chasing.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel: Could you please provide more color on environmental performance, particularly spills, incidents, and remediation efforts?

Lisa Harper: Hi Mike. We had just 12 spills totaling 420 barrels, a 65% volume cut, with top-tier response and recovery using advanced tools like skimmers and AI integrity management. This prevented hundreds of barrels and saved costs, strengthening our ESG standing. We're pushing harder with CCUS and monitoring for even better in 2024.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to David Reynolds for closing remarks.

David Reynolds: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
